name: Polyneuropathy associated with IgM monoclonal gammopathy with anti-MAG antibodies
aliases: IgM paraproteinemic neuropathy with anti-MAG antibodies

criteria.description: Symmetric distal sensory and motor neuropathy with predominant sensory ataxia
Presence of IgM monoclonal gammopathy in serum
Detection of anti-myelin-associated glycoprotein (anti-MAG) antibodies in serum
Nerve conduction studies showing demyelinating features with prolonged distal latencies and slowed conduction velocities
Nerve biopsy demonstrating demyelination with widening of myelin lamellae

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of symmetric distal neuropathy with IgM monoclonal gammopathy and positive anti-MAG antibodies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Nerve conduction studies and biopsy support diagnosis but are not mandatory if serology and clinical features are conclusive.

pathognomonic.notes: Severe impairment of proprioception leading to gait instability
searchTerms: loss of balance due to sensory loss in feet and hands
unsteady gait from numbness in limbs

pathognomonic.notes: Postural and kinetic tremor commonly observed

pathognomonic.symptomName: IgM monoclonal gammopathy with anti-MAG antibodies
searchTerms: IgM antibody disorder with nerve damage
numbness and tingling in hands and feet
pins and needles in fingers and toes
weak muscles in hands and feet
loss of strength in distal limbs
muscle weakness in arms and legs

common.symptomName: Hyporeflexia or areflexia in affected limbs

occasional.notes: Rare involvement of cranial nerves, e.g. facial weakness
Mild orthostatic hypotension or sweating abnormalities

rare.notes: Rarely associated with systemic manifestations like cryoglobulinemia
Very rare, may cause respiratory insufficiency
searchTerms: difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness

rare.notes: Rare cases with significant autonomic failure
searchTerms: severe nerve damage affecting automatic body functions

laboratory: Serum protein electrophoresis showing IgM monoclonal gammopathy
Normal or mildly elevated cerebrospinal fluid protein
imaging: Nerve ultrasound may show nerve enlargement
genetic: No known genetic mutations directly associated
other: Nerve conduction studies demonstrating demyelinating neuropathy
Nerve biopsy showing demyelination with widening of myelin lamellae

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of IgM monoclonal gammopathy and anti-MAG antibodies
More proximal weakness and relapsing-remitting course
Predominantly motor involvement without sensory ataxia
Presence of anti-GM1 antibodies instead of anti-MAG

redFlags: Rapidly progressive weakness or sensory loss
Development of systemic symptoms such as weight loss or night sweats
Respiratory muscle involvement or bulbar symptoms
references: Dalakas MC. Anti-MAG antibody neuropathy: an update. Neurology. 2019;92(24):1122-1130.
Nobile-Orazio E, et al. Diagnosis and treatment of IgM anti-MAG neuropathy. Nat Rev Neurol. 2020;16(9):511-525.
Orphanet: Polyneuropathy associated with IgM monoclonal gammopathy with anti-MAG antibodies. ORPHA:639.
